summary: Haya Akegarasu worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Otani University, Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, and under Manshi Kiyozawa, Kyoshi Takahama, and Shimei Futabatei. He held administrative leadership posts at Shinshu Otani-ha and Higashi Hongan-ji.
Heather Stoddard specializes in Tibetology and history/archaeology. She studied at SOAS University of London and under D. C. Lau, Samten Gyaltsen Karmay, and Nicole Vandier-Nicolas.

Heeraman Tiwari is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied at the universities of Lucknow, Delhi, and Oxford under Bimal Krishna Matilal and Richard Gombrich. He held positions at JNU, Heidelberg University, and Hebrew University of Jerusalem.
Hege Myrlund Larsen works in religious studies and Indology. She completed her PhD at the University of Bergen under the supervision of Bruce Kapferer (attested 2009).
Hegoda Khemananda worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. In 1993, he served as Vice Principal at Vidyodaya Pirivena and Director at Dharma Paryeshanalaya.

Heidi Fjeld works in Tibetology and religious studies. She studied at the University of Oxford and the University of Oslo under Signe Howell, later serving as a postdoctoral fellow at Oslo from around 2007 to 2010.
Heidi I. Koppl is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her MA at the University of Copenhagen under Christian K. Wedemeyer and also studied under Sherab Zangpo.

Heidi R. M. Pauwels works in Indology and religious studies. She studied at KU Leuven, Vrindaban Research Institute, University of Cologne, and University of Washington under Alan Entwistle. She held posts at SOAS and the University of Washington.

Heike Oberlin is an Indologist who studied at Kerala Kalamandalam and the universities of Tübingen and Würzburg. Her career includes posts at the University of Tübingen, Kerala Kalamandalam (2018), and Sapienza University of Rome (2025).
Heiner Eichner was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg under Karl Hoffmann and held a post at the University of Vienna from around 1989 to 2010.

Heinrich August Jäschke was a Tibetologist and linguist. He served as co-director at Pädagogium Niesky in 1847 and worked as a missionary for the Moravian Church and Moravian Mission in Kyelang from 1856/1857 to 1868.

Heinrich Blochmann worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and history/archaeology. He studied at Leipzig, Paris, and Calcutta under H. L. Fleischer and Karl Benedikt Hase, later holding posts at Doveton College, Aliah University, and The Asiatic Society.
Heinrich Brunn was a scholar in history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Bonn and held a post at the University of Munich from around 1865 to 1894.

Heinrich Ewald was a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and religious studies. Educated at the University of Göttingen under J. G. Eichhorn, T. C. Tychsen, G. J. Planck, and H. L. Planck, he held professorships at Göttingen and the University of Tübingen.
Heinrich Gustav Hotho worked in philosophy and other fields. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin from around 1820 to 1826 and subsequently held a post there from around 1829 to 1873.

Heinrich Hettrich worked in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Saarland University, Giessen, and Munich, later holding posts at Marburg and Würzburg, where he held the chair for comparative linguistics from 1989.

Heinrich Hübschmann was an Indologist, linguist, and Iranianist. He studied at Jena, Tübingen, Leipzig, and Munich under August Schleicher and Martin Haug. He held academic posts at the University of Leipzig and the University of Strasbourg.

Heinrich Kiepert was a geographer and historian who studied at Frederick William University Berlin and the University of Jena under August Boeckh and Julius Heinrich Petermann. He served at the Landes-Industrie-Comptoir and was a professor of geography in Berlin.

Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer was an orientalist and linguist. He studied at Leipzig and in Paris under Gottfried Hermann, Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy, Caussin de Perceval, and Antoine-Léonard Chézy, later holding the chair of oriental languages at Leipzig from 1836.

Heinrich Lüders was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Munich and Göttingen under Franz Kielhorn. He held posts at the Indian Institute in Oxford, Göttingen, Rostock, Kiel, Humboldt University of Berlin, and the Prussian Academy of Sciences.
